query: How can I inspect the changes staged for the next commit?

results.text:
Changes to be committed                   staged, ready for the next commit           green

  nothing to commit, working tree           everything is saved                         n/a
  clean

There is also a short format:       git status -s        prints  ??   for untracked,     M   for
modified (left column = staged, right column = not staged).

Staging changes:            git add

           Git Bash

  $ git add menu.txt
  $ git status
  On branch main

  No commits yet

6. Latest commit and the full commit history

  7. README.md is shown below the files: the project's front page

Some useful things to know:

   Press     t  on a repository page to search for a file, and              .   to open it in a web code
   editor.

   Click 🕒 commits to see the history (like                git log    ), and click any commit to see its
   diff (like   git show     ).

   Open a file and choose History (its commits) or Blame (who last changed each line).

Notice that after    git add    , plain  git diff     shows nothing: the change moved to the
staging area. Each form of       diff    compares two of the three stages:

  Command                                Compares

   git diff                              working directory ↔ staging area (unstaged changes)

   git diff --staged                     staging area ↔ last commit (what you're about to
                                         commit)
